artifacts.summary: All 7 phases complete: registry-derived gate-count expectations, two drift guards (G1/G2), and a permanent throwaway-gate fixture proof in both target suites, plus two collateral sites (crash net, cost model) fixed; redeployed with two documented, unrelated exclusions.

completion_data.completion_summary: Converted every hardcoded gate-count assertion in test-gate-registry-resolution.sh and test-verify-deploy-gate-selection.sh (plus the crash-net suite and measure-gate-costs.sh) to derive from the live gate registry, added gate_registry_max_id and gate_store_fixture_build as reusable primitives, added two cross-source drift guards (G1, G2), and proved the acceptance bar mechanically via a throwaway-gate fixture case in both suites. Directly fixed a real regression (test-verify-deploy-gate-selection.sh's case (c) went red mid-dispatch when a sibling task registered a real gate 27) and confirmed the fix in the final covering run. Deployed with two documented, confirmed-unrelated exclusions (a pre-existing gate10 timeout flake and two memory-extension doc violations).

memory_candidates.content: When a lint script validates something about verify-deploy.sh (e.g. lint-gate-registry.sh's Check A, 'every invoke function is defined'), it resolves its own target file relative to ITS OWN script location (${BASH_SOURCE[0]}), not from any data-file argument passed to it. Running the real lint-gate-registry.sh against a FIXTURE's gate-registry.data still checks the REAL verify-deploy.sh, not the fixture's -- to test a fixture's own internal consistency, run the fixture's own copied lint script, not the real one.

When building a test fixture that invokes verify-deploy.sh's gate-dispatch path for a single synthetic/throwaway gate id (not a full repo scan), pass the REAL repo root as TARGET rather than the fixture store's own root -- verify-deploy.sh refuses any TARGET without an existing deployed .claude/ tree before it reaches gate dispatch at all, and a minimal fixture-store builder correctly does not fabricate one. The throwaway gate's own body needs only the fixture's self-relative-resolved verify-deploy.sh/lib/data to carry the fixture shape; TARGET itself only needs to pass the entry check.

When converting a hardcoded test assertion to derive from a live data source, derive the expected value from a source INDEPENDENT of the function under test (e.g. a raw awk/grep re-read of the data file), never from the same accessor function the test is validating -- otherwise a broken accessor (bad sort, dropped entry) compares equal to itself and the assertion goes silently vacuous. Pair every such conversion with an explicit negative-control case demonstrating the comparison still discriminates (e.g. a synthetic copy with one entry removed).
